sanskrit: saṃ spṛśethāṃ tanūbhyāṃ saṃ mukhābhyāṃ sam ātmanā | saṃ vāṃ brahmaṇaspatiḥ somaḥ saṃ sparśayāti vām ||
english: May you two touch each other with your bodies, may you touch each other with your faces, with your very selves; Bṛhaspati and Soma bring you two into mutual contact.

sanskrit: abhy asya nāma vācā dadhāmi nāha mokṣyate | mamed ahainaṃ kāme labhai kṛṣṇam ivākhare ||
english: I fix his name upon him with my speech — he shall not be released from it; let me seize hold of him in longing, as one seizes a dark one in a muddy pit.

sanskrit: yaḥ premā preṇyām āsīd dattaḥ somena babhruṇā | tasmād adhi śrutaṃ mama mayy asya mana āhitam ||
english: The love-charm that was in the beloved one, bestowed by tawny Soma — from that charm, renowned above all others, his mind has been fixed upon me.

sanskrit: yaṃ pumāṃsaṃ kāmayase yasmin vā bhagam icchase | hṛcchokam asminn ā dadhmo yathā śuṣyāti tvām anu ||
english: Whatever man you desire, in whomsoever you wish to find your good fortune — in him we place a heart-burning, so that he shall pine away after you.

sanskrit: yathāsya hṛdayaṃ śuṣyād apicchinneva śaṃguṇī | cakṣur ākāśyaṃ bhīmaṃ māṃpaśyam abhirorudam ||
english: Just as his heart shall wither — like a string freshly severed — let his gaze grow terrible, sky-wide, and let him weep aloud, unable to see me.

sanskrit: priyaṃkaraṇam uttamaṃ madhughena tad ābhṛtam | tvaṃ hāsi varcasyo 'tho hāsi sumaṅgalaḥ | atho sarvāsāṃ vīrudhāṃ priyaṅkaraṇam ucyase ||
english: That supreme maker-of-love, brought here by the honey-licker — you indeed are possessed of radiance, and you indeed are truly auspicious; moreover, among all plants you are called the maker-of-love.

sanskrit: pratīcī somam asy oṣadhe pratīcy uta sūryam | pratīcī viśvān devāṃs tathā tvācchā vadāmasi ||
english: You, O herb, face Soma; you face likewise the sun; you face all the gods — so too we address you directly.

sanskrit: imāṃ khanāmy oṣadhiṃ nitatnīm anutantamām | āyataḥ pratinandanīṃ parāyato nivartanīm ||
english: I dig up this herb that spreads wide, that stretches along the ground — that which greets the one who comes, and turns back the one who departs.

sanskrit: amuṣyāhaṃ parāyata āyato mano agrabham | agrabhaṃ hastyaṃ mano 'tho hṛdayyaṃ manaḥ ||
english: Of yonder man, as he departs and as he comes, I have seized the mind; I have seized the mind that resides in his hand, and also the mind that dwells in his heart.

sanskrit: mayi te mana āhitaṃ mayi cittaṃ mayi vratam | mamed api kratāv aso mama citte sacāvahai ||
english: Upon me your mind is fixed, upon me your thought, upon me your vow; in my intention may you be, and together let us dwell in my heart.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vadāni mā tvaṃ sabhāyāṃ gha tvaṃ vada | mamed asas tvaṃ kevalo nānyāsāṃ kīrtayāś cana ||
english: Let me speak — not you; in the assembly, you shall not speak; let you be mine alone, and do not praise any other woman.

sanskrit: yadi vāsi tiro janaṃ yadi vā nadyas tiraḥ | iyaṃ tvā mahyam oṣadhir baddhveva ny ānayāt ||
english: Whether you be beyond the folk, or whether you be beyond the rivers — let this herb bring you back to me, as if binding you and leading you home.

sanskrit: saṃ rājāno 'guḥ sam ṛṇāny aguḥ saṃ kuṣṭhā aguḥ saṃ kulā aguḥ | sam asmāsu suṣvapnyaṃ nir dviṣate duṣvapnyaṃ suvāmaḥ ||
english: Kings have gone to union, debts have gone to union, skin-diseases have gone to union, clans have gone to union; toward us let good dreams be gathered together — we drive the ill dream away to the one who hates us.

sanskrit: devānāṃ patnīnāṃ garbha yamasya karaṇaḥ | yo bhadraḥ svapnaḥ sa mama yaḥ pāpas taṃ dviṣate pra hiṇmaḥ ||
english: O Embryo of the wives of the gods, O instrument of Yama — whatever dream is auspicious, that is mine; whatever is evil, that we dispatch to the one who hates us.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇāmā nāmāsi kṛṣṇaśakuner mukhaṃ nirṛter mukham | taṃ tvā svapna tathā vidma ||
english: Tṛṣṇāman is your name; you are the face of the dark bird, the face of Nirṛti — thus we know you, O Dream, for what you are.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ svapnāśva ivākāyam aśva iva nīnāham | anāsmākaṃ devapīyuṃ piyāruṃ vapsaḥ ||
english: You, O Dream, carry off the bodiless one as a horse carries a load; like a horse you have dragged us in the night — carry off the god-reviler, the slanderer, who is not ours.

sanskrit: yad asmāsu duṣvapnyaṃ yad goṣu yac ca no gṛhe | anāsmākas tad devapīyuḥ piyāruṃ niṣkam iva prati muñcatām ||
english: Whatever ill dream there is among us, whatever among our cattle, and whatever in our house — the god-reviler and slanderer who is not ours: let him be released with that, as one releases a necklace-amulet.

sanskrit: navāratnīn avamāya- -asmākaṃ tanvas pari | duṣvapnyaṃ sarvaṃ durbhūtaṃ dviṣate nir diśāmasi ||
english: Measuring off nine cubits away from our bodies — all ill dream, all ill omen, we consign to the one who hates us.
